findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences undefined destination calendar
findings.body: After destinationCalendar became an array, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when the event has no destination calendar. The next line still reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` whenever the location is MeetLocationType. Any Google Meet event without a destination calendar now throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Guard the access or use optional chaining.

findings.title: Video booking references lose credentialId
findings.body: In create(), referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Video results previously kept `result.credentialId`. Without a credentialId on the video booking reference, handleCancelBooking's video cancellation branch (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`) is skipped, so the video meeting is not deleted when the booking is cancelled. Preserve `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

findings.title: externalId is dropped before creating calendar events
findings.body: createEvent now accepts an externalId argument, and EventManager passes `destination.externalId` so each destination should create its event on that calendar. But this call still invokes `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and never forwards externalId; it only copies externalId into the returned result. Google uses credentialId to pick the right destination, but Office365, Lark and BaseCalendarService all read `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event with multiple hosts, every service call therefore uses the first host's calendar: the second Office365/Lark event fails or is created in the wrong calendar, and CalDAV silently creates nothing. Pass the destination externalId or make every service select by credentialId.

findings.title: Team destination calendars dropped when organizer destination is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The following `if (COLLECTIVE) evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing in that case, so destination calendars collected from other hosts are discarded. A collective event whose organizer has no destination calendar but whose other hosts do will not invite those hosts. Initialize the array before pushing.

findings.title: Organization slug condition flipped
findings.body: The spread condition for `slug` was changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. With team billing disabled (the self-hosted/default case), organizations are now created without a slug, breaking organization URLs. With billing enabled, the code now writes both `slug` and `requestedSlug`, changing the deferred-slug flow. This unrelated change should be reverted or explicitly justified.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback matches externalId against null
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null/empty, updateEvent and deleteEvent fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since externalCalendarId is falsy, this searches for a destination with a null/empty externalId and normally returns undefined. updateEvent then calls Google without a calendarId, and deleteEvent falls back to deleting from `primary`. Previously the code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Use the first destination calendar or select by credential as the fallback.

findings.title: Only first old calendar event deleted when merging bookings
findings.body: The method now processes all calendar references for the new booking, but the `newBookingId` merge cleanup still calls `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes a single old calendar event. For collective bookings with multiple calendar references, the remaining hosts' old events are left on their calendars after reschedule/merge. Loop over all old calendar references and delete each one.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation still only uses booking owner credentials
findings.body: In the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch, the code still iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and picks the first calendar reference from each updated booking, rather than using the current reference's credentialId/externalCalendarId. For collective recurring bookings, calendar events belonging to other hosts are not deleted. The new outer loop over bookingCalendarReference also re-runs this same deletion for every reference, causing duplicate delete attempts. Use the current reference to delete the matching event for each updated booking.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose calendar external id and credential id
findings.body: referencesToCreate in updateLocation now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult never populates either field. For calendar update results these values are undefined, so editLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId; later updates or cancellations must fall back to primary/all credentials. The old code used evt.destinationCalendar for these values. Either populate them in CalendarManager.updateEvent or keep the destination fallback.
